Let’s talk about Chapter 8: Adapting the Framework to Different People and Situations.
You know, no two teams—or individuals—are exactly the same. While the basics—like setting clear goals, offering immediate praise, and giving quick corrections—work everywhere, how you put these into action really depends on who you’re working with.
That’s where great leaders stand out—they’re flexible. They pay attention, get curious, and tweak their approach to fit the unique mix of personalities and needs on their team.
Think about this: Some people light up when they’re recognized in front of everyone, while others would much rather have a quiet “well done” in private. There are folks who want every detail spelled out, and others who just want the big picture so they can run with it. The secret? Ask questions, listen, and be willing to adjust.
Here are a few simple ways you can personalize your approach:
Ask your team how they like to get feedback and recognition. Some might want a shoutout in a meeting; others, just a personal note.
Pay attention to how often you check in—and make it fit each person’s needs. Maybe one teammate wants regular touchpoints, while another prefers more space.
And don’t forget about cultural differences. The way praise or correction is received can really vary, so it helps to be mindful of those nuances.
Imagine a project team that includes both seasoned pros and brand-new hires. The manager lays out clear, shared goals for everyone, but checks in more regularly with the newcomers, giving them extra support and encouragement. For the veterans, there’s more freedom and recognition of their expertise. And when challenges pop up, the feedback is tailored—maybe more hands-on for someone just starting, and more collaborative for those with experience.
This kind of flexibility matters in all sorts of workplaces. In a high-speed environment, feedback might need to be even quicker and more to the point. In creative fields, goals might be broader, leaving more room to experiment. The core ideas stay the same, but the details? They shift, depending on the situation.
When leaders adapt the framework to fit their people and their context, it shows real respect for individual differences—and that’s what creates a space where everyone can thrive. This responsiveness doesn’t just boost trust; it helps teams handle change and uncertainty with a lot more confidence.
